stem: A foreign government offers gifts to employees of a Philippine agency. Under Section 7(d) of RA 6713, Congress consents to only certain kinds of gifts from foreign governments. Which of these may an employee accept?
choices: A gold watch worth ₱80,000, given as a souvenir
A ₱50,000 cash gift to thank the agency for its help
A fellowship grant to study in that country
Free travel and hotels for a trip within the Philippines
answer: A fellowship grant to study in that country
hints: Section 7(d) lists three kinds of foreign gifts that may be accepted. Anything not on the list is not allowed.

The list: (i) a gift "of nominal value" as a souvenir or mark of courtesy; (ii) a scholarship, fellowship grant or medical treatment; (iii) travel that takes place entirely outside the Philippines, if the head of office permits it.

Test each choice against the list. A souvenir or mark of courtesy must be of nominal (very small) value. Travel must be entirely outside the Philippines. A gift that fits none of the three items is not allowed. Pick the one choice that passes.

steps.action: Read the list in Section 7(d). As to gifts from foreign governments, Congress consents to: (i) "a gift of nominal value tendered and received as a souvenir or mark of courtesy"; (ii) "a gift in the nature of a scholarship or fellowship grant or medical treatment"; (iii) travel grants or expenses for travel that takes place entirely outside the Philippines, if appropriate and "permitted by the head of office."
steps.why: Consent means permission. Nominal value means a very small, token value.

steps.action: Gold watch worth ₱80,000: a souvenir is allowed only if it is of nominal value. ₱80,000 is not nominal, so it fails item (i).
₱50,000 cash gift: it is not a scholarship, fellowship, medical treatment or travel grant. As a mark of courtesy under item (i), it would have to be of nominal value, and ₱50,000 is not. So it fails.
Trip within the Philippines: item (iii) covers only travel entirely outside the Philippines, so it fails.
Fellowship grant: it matches item (ii) exactly.
The answer is: A fellowship grant to study in that country.

trapNotes.A gold watch worth ₱80,000, given as a s: Souvenirs are allowed only if they are "of nominal value." An ₱80,000 gold watch is far from nominal.
trapNotes.A ₱50,000 cash gift to thank the agency: A thank-you gift could only fit item (i), which requires "a gift of nominal value." ₱50,000 in cash is not nominal, and it is not a scholarship, fellowship, medical treatment or travel grant.
trapNotes.Free travel and hotels for a trip within: Item (iii) covers only travel that takes place entirely outside the Philippines. A trip within the country is not covered.
